title: OCR Agent output, version 1
description: What the OCR Agent read off a package, exactly as printed. This file is sent to the model verbatim as a structured-output schema AND is the contract for what lands in submissions.ocr_output — one file, so the two cannot drift. Two consequences of being the request schema: it stays inside the API's supported JSON Schema subset (no minimum/maximum, no minLength, no recursion, additionalProperties false on every object), so the 0-to-1 bound on confidence is stated in prose and enforced in PHP rather than by the schema; and every field is required, with null as the way to say 'not readable', because an omitted key and an unreadable field are different claims. Nothing here is normalized — resolving 'HW' to 'Hot Wheels' is the Metadata Agent's job, and it can only do it if this layer reports what the card actually says.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema. Stored alongside the output so a later reader can tell which shape it is looking at without guessing from the keys.

brand.description: The toy manufacturer's brand printed on the packaging — Hot Wheels, Matchbox, Tomica. NOT the real car's manufacturer: a Hot Wheels Honda Civic has brand 'Hot Wheels', not 'Honda'.

year.description: The model year printed on the packaging, as a four-digit number. Not the copyright year in the small print, which is often different.

series.description: The named release wave printed on the card, such as 'Night Burnerz' or 'HW Exotics'. Null if the packaging names no series.

casting_name.description: The model's name as printed, including any leading year abbreviation and punctuation — "'92 Honda Prelude", not "1992 Honda Prelude".

collector_number.description: The collector number as printed, keeping the separator — '160/244'. A string, not a number, because the printed form carries the series size.

toy_number.description: The manufacturer's alphanumeric product code from the small print, usually on the back — e.g. 'T9765'.

confidence.description: Per-field certainty that the reported value matches the printed text, each between 0 and 1 inclusive. Per-field rather than one score for the whole read, because a card can have a crisp brand logo and an illegible toy number, and the Review Agent needs to tell those apart. A field reported as null scores 0.
